subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `memorySearch` exclusion/path-hygiene contract now, and should it cover builtin indexing only or also QMD, status diagnostics, and benchmark-contamination docs?
rationale: This cannot be resolved as a narrow bug fix because it adds public config and changes which files enter durable recall context, while repository policy treats config and memory/session-state surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Land the open `excludePaths` PR or successor after fixing merge semantics and index identity, while documenting builtin-only scope and tracking QMD/diagnostic parity separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause the open PR until builtin indexing, QMD, watcher behavior, status diagnostics, docs, and stale-index cleanup share one accepted exclusion model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and improve memory status/docs guidance around path drift, broad `extraPaths`, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Land the open `excludePaths` PR or successor after fixing merge semantics and index identity, while documenting builtin-only scope and tracking QMD/diagnostic parity separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory host SDK and manager-state history makes this the strongest available owner for the config/runtime boundary decision.
